title_raw: Director and Professor, The Sanford School

areas_raw: My research focuses on scale development and educational assessment practices. In particular, I have published articles on (a) the assessment of children's social skills and academic competence, (b) the use of testing accommodations and alternate assessment methods for evaluating the academic performance of students with disabilities for educational accountability, and (c) students’ opportunities to learn the intended curriculum. In the process of conducting my research, I have developed a number of measurement tools that are now used in schools and clinics across the country. Specifically, with colleagues I have authored the Social Skills Rating System (SSRS), the Socials Skills Improvement System (SSiS), and My Instructional Learning Opportunity Guidance System (MyiLOGS). Along with Vanderbilt colleagues, I also designed and validated the Vanderbilt Assessment of Leadership in Education (VAL-ED) to evaluate the performance of principals and their influence on students’ achievement.

areas_raw: Her program of research focuses on the socio-emotional development of young children, particularly the relations of children’s self-regulation abilities (i.e., effortful control) to children’s social adjustment. Further, much of her work has examined the role that parenting plays in the development of young children’s moral development, altruism, and empathy. Dr. Spinrad has published numerous peer-reviewed journal articles and chapters on the contributions of self-regulation and parenting to children’s moral behavior and social adjustment.

areas_raw: Professor White is an expert in youth development, particularly in how socio-emotional and socio-cognitive development unfolds across time and in the context of exposures to both proximal (e.g., family, community) and more distal (e.g., national policy) factors. Her work also supports methodological advances, helping to define the characteristics and features of higher-quality scientific inquiry, especially with populations who have been underserved by the psychological and developmental sciences. With over 80 publications and national and international recognition for her contributions to advancing the science of child development, her scholarship documents the contextual challenges and opportunities today's U.S. youth face and how such factors combine to promote or inhibit their adjustment and mental health.
